subject: Anthropology
title: Stigma and Illness
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Stigma and Illness.

hook.text: A person with HIV hides their diagnosis. A person with cancer gets sympathy. Why do some illnesses carry shame?

buildup.text: Stigma is the social shame attached to certain conditions — marking sufferers as damaged, dangerous, or morally flawed.

discovery.text: Goffman showed that stigma spoils identity. The stigmatized person is reduced from a whole person to a single flaw.

twist.text: Stigma is never about the disease itself. It reflects cultural values about purity, morality, and who deserves sympathy.

climax.text: Stigma kills as surely as disease. It prevents people from seeking care, disclosing illness, or finding support.

punchline.text: The label can hurt more than the disease.

quiz.question: What does stigma do to illness?
options: It prevents people from seeking care by attaching social shame
It has no real effect on health

details.summary: Stigma attached to certain diseases — HIV, leprosy, mental illness, epilepsy — adds social suffering to physical suffering. Stigmatized patients face discrimination, isolation, and shame that can be more devastating than the disease itself.
details.whyItMatters: Stigma is a major barrier to treatment-seeking and adherence worldwide. People hide symptoms, avoid clinics, and refuse diagnosis to escape the social consequences that certain disease labels carry.
takeaways: Disease stigma adds social suffering to physical illness
Stigma deters treatment-seeking and medication adherence
Social consequences of diagnosis can exceed medical consequences

faq.question: Why are certain diseases more stigmatized than others?
faq.answer: Diseases associated with moral failing (HIV linked to sexual behavior), contagion fear (leprosy), or mental difference (schizophrenia) attract the most stigma. Stigma increases when disease is perceived as the patient's fault or when it threatens community boundaries.

faq.question: How does stigma affect public health efforts?
faq.answer: HIV stigma delayed testing and treatment uptake for decades. Mental illness stigma prevents millions from seeking care. TB stigma leads patients to hide symptoms until they become contagious. Effective public health must address stigma alongside biological disease to succeed.
